chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from al-Fadl ibn Uthman, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not upon the people of the Qibla except the sighting; it is not upon the Muslims except the sighting.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْقِبْلَةِ: People of the Qibla — all those who pray facing Mecca, a classical term encompassing all Muslims
key_terms.الرُّؤْيَةُ: The sighting — specifically the visual sighting of the crescent moon (hilal) as the legal criterion for month-commencement
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِلَّا: Negation of obligation except — a legal formula denoting that only one criterion applies

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about crescent moon sighting for determining Islamic months?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) enunciates a principle regarding the crescent moon sighting (ru'yah) as the criterion for the beginning of Islamic months, particularly Ramadan and Shawwal. The statement distinguishes between two groups — 'the people of the Qibla' (a broad term for all who pray toward Mecca, i.e., all Muslims) and 'the Muslims' — both of whom are bound only by the ru'yah (sighting of the crescent) as a communal obligation. In the jurisprudential context of early Islamic law, this teaching addressed debates about whether calculation, estimation, or individual personal sighting could substitute for communal ru'yah.
